payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: pass: The mug is visibly to the right of the headphones. fail: The mug is visibly not to the right of the headphones. unknown: Their relative positions cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Inspect the edited image and compare the mug’s position with the headphones; this directly tests the requested outcome.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.

fulfillment: The node overweights the final-state relation and treats any positional change as progress. In the source, the mug is already left of the headphones; in the edit, the rightmost mug is right of them, but the image also shows an additional mug and a blurred mug-shaped remnant at the original location. Do not infer completion from “a mug” being right of the headphones: bind the same source mug across images and assess whether that object was moved, while accounting for duplication/remnant and uncertainty. The trace’s two pass observations do not establish that the requested object was moved or that the edit is complete; distinguish evidence of progress from evidence of fulfillment under the rubric, and lower confidence or return unknown if identity/change cannot be resolved. This is a semantic evidence/criterion issue, not a transport or schema failure.
s2: The binding is too vague to distinguish the original mug from newly rendered copies. Make the check track the source mug’s visual identity and location across the two images, then assess whether that same object moved toward the requested right-of-headphones position; a mug merely appearing on the right is not evidence that the source mug moved. In this edit, the rightmost mug is right of the headphones, but the source mug’s original area contains a blurred mug-shaped remnant and another mug appears near the headphones, so do not treat the final relation alone as proof of movement or completion. Keep this node focused on progress evidence, separate from the fulfillment decision, and use unknown or reduced confidence when object correspondence or change is visually ambiguous. This is a semantic binding/evidence issue, not a transport or schema failure.

response.content: {"text":"The check is bound only to the edited image’s final relation, so it can pass when a mug appears to the right even though the requested source mug was not cleanly moved. Bind the mug across source and edit using visual identity and compare its location; assess evidence of movement/progress separately from whether the requested final placement is fulfilled. Here the source mug is left of the headphones, while the edit shows a blurred mug-shaped remnant at its original location and multiple mugs, including one to the right. Treat these as ambiguity about correspondence and possible duplication—not proof either that the source mug moved or that no progress occurred. Calibrate confidence or return unknown when identity/change cannot be resolved, and avoid a high-confidence pass based solely on the right-side mug. This is a semantic binding and evidence-criterion issue, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure."}
